LESSON: PHONOLOGICAL AWARENESS: ARTICULATION

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: ARABIC LANGUAGE
Strand: Listening and Speaking
Topic 1.4: Phonological Awareness: Articulation
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Phonological Awareness: Articulation, part of Listening and Speaking in Grade 5 ARABIC LANGUAGE.

Key inquiry question: Why do we greet one another? 2. How do letters differ from sounds?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. work with peers to match sounds to letters to form syllables,

2. combine syllables to syllables to form meaningful words,

3. pronounce words with sound baa, mim, lam, dal from a given display in pairs,

4. imitate using the pronouns hadaa, hadhihi ,

5. practise using Arabic greetings such as assalamu-alaikum, keif- haluka/halaki,

6. collaborate with peers to role-play formal and informal greetings. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. work with peers to match sounds to letters to form syllables,
2. combine syllables to syllables to form meaningful words,
3. pronounce words with sound baa, mim, lam, dal from a given display in pairs,
4. imitate using the pronouns hadaa, hadhihi ,
5. practise using Arabic greetings such as assalamu-alaikum, keif- haluka/halaki,
6. collaborate with peers to role-play formal and informal greetings. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Phonological Awareness: Articulation together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and collaboration: This is developed as the learner builds on their interaction skills by practising using

Arabic greetings such as assalamu-alaikum, keif-haluka/halaki.

• Self-efficacy: This is promoted as the learner sharpens their conversational skills when collaborating with peers to role-play

formal and informal greetings.

Values:
Respect: This is enhanced as the learner appreciates the efforts made by peers when collaborating to role play formal and

informal greetings.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Cultural awareness is promoted as the learner appreciates and practices various formal and informal greetings used among

various people at different times.

Link to Other Learning Areas:

The learner is able to relate the concept of greetings and introductions to similar concepts as taught in English.
